architecture: pnpm monorepo with three packages — Next.js 14 frontend (apps/web), Colyseus WebSocket game server (apps/server), and a shared TypeScript types package (packages/types). The frontend renders 3D gameplay via React Three Fiber, while the server runs a 60fps authoritative game loop that syncs state to all clients via Colyseus schema patching.
keyPatterns: Server-authoritative multiplayer — clients send input messages, the server validates and updates state, and Colyseus binary delta encoding pushes only changed fields to all players. Client state managed by three Zustand stores (game logic, Colyseus connection, multiplayer helpers). 3D rendering uses React Three Fiber with 18 custom hooks for player controls, character animations, physics, collision detection, and position interpolation.
notableDetails: Dynamic math challenge generation system that scales difficulty per level. Modular cash/scoring system with per-number earnings, health bonuses, and time bonuses. Character system with selectable models, skeletal animations, and smooth crossfade transitions. Graceful server shutdown that warns active players and lets games finish. Howler.js for spatial audio.

architecture: Next.js 16 (App Router) with React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. Section-based single-page layout driven by JSON data files — components map over the data rather than hardcoding content. Deployed on Vercel.
keyPatterns: Three.js via React Three Fiber powers multiple 3D experiences — the animated Shroom Wizard model (GLTF with 11 animations), a 3D testimonials carousel (Canvas 2D rendered to Three.js sphere geometry), and particle effects. Framer Motion handles DOM animations and scroll-triggered reveals. The AI chat uses Claude Haiku via Anthropic SDK on a Next.js API route with Upstash Redis rate limiting (per-IP daily cap and global token budget).
notableDetails: Shroom Mode psychedelic effect uses SVG feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap filters with a 30-second intensity ramp, applied to a wrapper div so the music player stays undistorted. Custom Web Audio API music player with real-time frequency visualization (bass, treble, and intensity bands). The wizard has a two-mode persona — Mystic Voice for banter, Clear Speech for career facts — with a tool-use mechanism that triggers an interactive mushroom ceremony UI.

architecture: An Expo app (iOS) and a Next.js web app sharing a tRPC API on Neon Postgres.
keyPatterns: The coach is a Vercel AI SDK agent on Claude. It holds the user's whole training history and changes the program through typed tools, with an auditable decision log.
notableDetails: AI strength coach for iOS and web: voice logging, Apple Health sync and offline replay. On TestFlight.

architecture: A Turborepo monorepo: the resume is YAML, checked by a Zod schema, rendered by React and printed to PDF with Playwright, with 0-pixel parity tests. The editor is Next.js 16 on Neon Postgres with Better Auth.
keyPatterns: The AI is routed by task: Opus for writing, Sonnet for chat, Haiku for quick edits. A career bank of sourced facts backs the writing: a deterministic grounding check requires citations, and every number has to trace back to a fact.
notableDetails: An AI resume builder, in development and invite-only. It tailors a resume per job posting and flags any line nothing backs.

architecture: Plain TypeScript on one raw WebGL2 canvas on this site: spring soft bodies per word, a glyph atlas and skinned GLB characters, with custom physics and Web Audio.
keyPatterns: Lazy chunks, paused while hidden, and never mounted for reduced motion.
notableDetails: The hero photo dissolves into a copy of Phill's resume you can knock apart. Play mode reads its level off the resume's text lines (one-way platforms, role checkpoints, Impact coins) and turns it into a run from his name to the last line.

architecture: A pnpm monorepo: a pure, deterministic 60 Hz simulation package (the rules, the ball, the players, rally scoring to 11, win by 2) and a Vite + TypeScript web app that draws it with plain three.js from a sideline camera.
keyPatterns: The sim is pure and seeded, so a match replays bit-exact from its inputs; CPU players run on the same sim, and replays print a point-by-point timeline for debugging. The characters are modular voxel figures built in code: species presets mixed with outfit kits.
notableDetails: Wacky arcade pickleball in the NBA Jam mould, in development: local matches against the CPU work today, online play and touch controls are next. Players who get hit by the ball explode into cubes and rebuild.
